ActorKind.description:
Who a PR's author or merger was, by the git host's account type: git authorship can't tell, because agents commit
under the person's own identity.

oneOf.description: The merge train (merger only).
No git host to ask, or it didn't say.

AgentBlock.description: An agent at work: the client fills in its live state. Exactly one of `taskId` and `threadRef`.

AgentsCapData.description:
`agents.cap` data: a project's max agents or the fleet cap changed. The event's summary is the one quiet line its
chat shows.

paused.description: Agents told to push their work and wait (`pauseExtras`).

running.description: The project's agents (or, for the fleet cap, every slot) running and queued just after the change.

AppPresenceData.description:
`app.presence`: the app was focused on a project's screen (the event's machine and project) with input in the
last 60 s, for one interval. Only that: never keystrokes or content. At most one per minute per key.

fromMs.description: Epoch milliseconds on the hub clock.

AskBlock.description:
A question for the human, as buttons: Approve and Deny without `options`, one of `options` with them. The
answer is the human's chat reply (`chat_send` with the button's label as its text), so only the human answers
it; an agent's message never does. A command that needs approval still goes through `gated_run`.

AttachmentBlock.description: An image or clip already uploaded to the hub: its bytes come from `attachment_get`.

AttachmentRef.description: A file on a message: what the app shows without fetching it. Its bytes come from `attachment_get`.

message.description: git's first line, e.g. "fatal: Authentication failed for 'https://github.com/a/b.git/'"; "offline".

BaseErrorKind.description: Why a worktree's base may be behind its remote's default branch.

oneOf.description: The remote can't be reached, or didn't answer in time.
The remote refused git's credentials; the agent's pushes will fail the same way.
The remote says there is no such repository: a wrong URL or name, or credentials that can't see it.
git can't run ssh on the machine: it isn't installed. The doctor shows it; no attention item.
The remote answered but names no default branch: its HEAD points at a branch it doesn't have.
The project has no remote: the base is a local branch.
Any other fetch failure.

BrowserControl.description:
Who drives a live session's browser. A person takes it over (human) and hands it back (handing_back, until the
agent's next tool call sees the page as the person left it, then agent). While it isn't the agent's, the agent's
browser tools answer that a person has control.

BrowserSessionEventData.description:
`browser.session`: a session started, changed hands, ended or its recording landed. The rest comes from
`browser_sessions`.

BrowserSessionState.description:
Where a session is. live → uploading → recorded; lost when the node could not record or upload it; expired once
retention deleted its recording (its row stays).

reason.description: Why it moved, when the train says: always set when a pass hands it back to `ready` (a bounce).

ChartBlock.description: A line, bar or area chart: `x` labels along the bottom, one value per label in each series.

oneOf.description:
An agent or integration writing with its own key (`fleetd chat` with an agent key): input for the lead, never
the human. It approves nothing, answers nothing that is the human's, and leaves needs-you as it was.
fleetd itself: one-line events (a PR merged, an agent started, a past order's state).

ChatBlock.description:
One block: `v`, the block schema's version (`BLOCK_VERSION`), and its kind's fields. A kind or version a client
doesn't know shows as the part's text.

ChatClient.description: Where a human message was written.

oneOf.description: The desktop app.
`fleetd chat`.

ChatDelivery.description: How a human message reached the lead.

oneOf.description: The lead was idle: the message started its next turn.
The lead was mid-turn: it takes the message at its next step, as a steer.
The lead was mid-turn and the human asked for now: its running step stopped for the message.
The lead is starting, or its machine is away: the message waits and goes in as soon as it can.

ChatHistorySource.description:
Where a history message came from, for messages from before the chat existed (a read model; nothing is moved or
destroyed). Absent on messages written in the chat.

oneOf.description: An order's text as it was submitted.
A person's note on an order.
A person's steer to the lead or one of its agents.
What the lead said in its own session.
An order's outcome (done, stopped, failed) as a one-line event.
A question the lead asked with the retired questions tool, and its answer.

ChatItem.description: The two things a chat can't carry as plain text, shown inline in place of the message text.

by.description: The name of the key that wrote it: a person's device for a human message, the agent for an agent's.

client.description: A human message: where it was written.

clientRequestId.description: A human message: the `clientRequestId` its `chat_send` carried, for the app's optimistic copy.

delivery.description: A human message: how it reached the lead.

history.description: From before the chat: where this history message came from.

parts.description:
A final lead message of more than one bubble, or with a block: its bubbles in order. Absent: `text` is one
bubble (and while a message streams).

person.description: A human message: the person who wrote it. Absent from a hub before people.

previewSuggestion.description:
An agent's suggestion to try a PR (preview_suggest), posted once per PR with `text` in its words: the app
shows it as one line with Try it. Nothing runs from it.

remembered.description: A system line "Remembered: …": what the lead's `remember` wrote, which `memory_undo` takes back.

replyTo.description: A human message: the bubble it answers.

skills.description: A human message: the skills it named with `$name`, which the lead's copy lists.

text.description: Markdown. Empty while a streamed message has no text yet, and for an inline `item`.

updatedAt.description: Set when the text was last appended to, or an item's state changed.

ChatMessageEventData.description:
`chat.message` data: on each new message, and again when a streamed message is final or an inline item changes
state. `message` is the whole message when it fits the event's 2 KB; otherwise read it with `chat_history`
(`after: seq - 1`, `limit: 1`).

oneOf.description: The lead is still writing it: `chat_delta` frames append to its text until it is `final`.

ChatOpenItem.description: An inline item that waits on the human: which message, and what it asks for.

ChatPart.description:
One bubble of a lead message: `text.slice(start, end)` (UTF-16 offsets, like `ChatDelta.offset`), shown as
markdown, or as `block` when it has one (the slice is then the block's fence, its readable fallback).

ChatReplyTo.description:
The bubble a human message answers: a lead message and the bubble's place in it, as `parts` counts (0 for a
message of one bubble). The lead reads that bubble whole over the reply, and when it was written.

ChecklistChangedData.description: `checklist.changed`. The items are not in the event; checklist_get reads them.

by.description: The lead (`lead:<machine>/<project>`) or a person (`human:<key name>`).

person.description: The person who changed it (`checklist_edit`), removals included; absent when the lead did.

requiredChecks.description: Status checks the default branch requires, from branch protection and rulesets.

workflows.description: Active GitHub Actions workflows by name (from `.github/workflows` on a checkout without GitHub access).

CiMainData.description: `ci.main`: main-branch CI of a train repo changed state.

oneOf.description: Not fetched since the hub started. Also what a state this build doesn't know decodes as.
A person's own session (Claude Code over MCP, or the CLI).
Anything else holding an agent key.
A project's lead, holding work in reserve.
Its work reached the base.
Its owner dropped it.
Not renewed for `CLAIM_TTL_MS`.
Before git reports anything.
"Receiving objects".
"Resolving deltas".
"Updating files".
The clone finished; the hub reads the default branch, CI and merge rules.

CloneProgressData.description:
`HubEvent.data` on `project.clone_progress`: on each phase change and its 100 %, else every 5 percent at most once
a second.

detail.description: As git prints it, e.g. "12.40 MiB | 3.10 MiB/s".

CommandApprovalItem.description:
A risky command (prod write, spend, delete, credential use), a session's permission prompt or an agent's proposed
preview setting waits for the human: exactly what it would do, then Approve or Deny. Answered with
`approval_answer`, naming `requestId`. Exactly one of `gated`, `permission` and `previewConfig`.

by.description: The key name of the person who answered.

finishedAt.description: Once it ran or failed: when the result came back.

gated.description: A gated command: exactly what runs once approved.

machineId.description: Where it runs, or the machine of the session that asks.

note.description: Why it is open again ("not run: the node was offline when approved"), or why it failed without running.

outputTail.description: The end of the output, once it ran.

permission.description: A session's permission prompt: the tool and what it would do.

previewConfig.description:
An agent's proposed preview setting (preview_config_propose): approved, it becomes the project's `preview`.
Older apps show it as an approval with neither command nor permission.
Boxed: the setting is large beside the item's other fields, and every chat item would carry its size.

oneOf.description: Approved and run: see `exitCode` and `outputTail`.
Approved, and the node could not run it.

CommitSha.description: Full lowercase hex commit SHA, 40 or 64 characters

DeliveredHow.description: How a delivered steer was taken in.

oneOf.description: It started a turn while the agent was idle.
After the running tool returned.
⌘Enter stopped the running step (`stoppedTool` names it).
An older claude merged it into the running turn; the ack rule catches a miss.

DiffBlock.description: Changes to show: the files with their hunks, or a PR whose diff the client reads. Exactly one of the two.

hunks.description: Unified-diff hunks, each from its `@@` line.

FetchFailedData.description: `project.fetch_failed` data: the start that found the remote unfetchable.

fix.description: A command for a person to run, e.g. "gh auth login".

message.description: The whole line, which the summary may cut: what failed, the fix, and where agents start from meanwhile.

GatedRunSpec.description: Stored with the approval and never changed: the human approves exactly these bytes.

LandingRoute.description: How a commit reached a base branch.

oneOf.description: Merged by fleetd's merge train.
A PR or merge request merged outside the train.
Pushed straight to the base.

paused.description: true: new agents wait; false: they start again.

oneOf.description: `user.md`: how the human works across every project.
This project's `MEMORY.md`, or one of its topic files.

MergeRules.description: How the default branch may be merged into.

protected.description: Branch protection or an active ruleset applies to the default branch.

requiredReviews.description: Approving reviews a pull request needs.

rulesets.description: Active rulesets that apply to the default branch, by name.

squashAllowed.description: Absent when gh could not read the repository settings.

strict.description: Pull requests must be up to date with the base before merging.

by.description: Who made the change; absent for the hub machine's own CLI and for a device joining.

PersonRef.description:
Who did something, with their name at the time: on chat messages, approvals, secrets, decisions and checklist
changes.

PrBlock.description: A pull request: the client fills in its live state (title, checks, review, merged) from the hub.

title.description: Shown until the live title is known.

PreviewConfig.description:
A project's preview setting (Settings › Projects › Try it, or `project_settings_set {preview}`). Nothing runs
because of it: it says how to run a preview someone asks for.

idleMinutes.description: A preview no one used for this many minutes ends.

PreviewConfigProposeCall.description:
`preview_config_propose`: how to run the project's preview, for the person to approve as a card in the chat.
Nothing is saved until they do. Answered with the request, as `gated_run` is.

PreviewEventData.description: `preview.state`: a preview started, moved a step, became ready, ended or failed. previews_list reads the rest.

PreviewOf.description: What a preview is of: one PR, or an order's PRs merged together onto their base on a scratch branch (D162).

oneOf.description: Checking out, setting up, building or starting: `steps` says which.
It answers: the person can use it.
Thrown away: its processes, port and worktree are gone. `endReason` says why.
A step failed: `steps` names it with the end of its output. Nothing of it runs.

PreviewSuggestion.description: An agent's suggestion to try a PR: one line with a Try it button, once per PR. Nothing runs from it.

why.description: Why a person should try it, in a line.

ProjectAddFailedData.description: `HubEvent.data` on `project.add_failed`: a clone that was accepted, then failed.

ProjectAddedData.description: `HubEvent.data` on `project.added`, for every add (a path or a clone).

addId.description: Absent when the add registered an existing directory.

created.description: False when the directory was already a project.

inspect.description: Long lists are cut so the event fits the log's 2 KB of data; `project_add` with `dryRun` returns them whole.

ProjectChatState.description: One chat's state, for the sidebar and the status row.

lastSeq.description: The newest message's `seq`; 0 for an empty chat.

needsYou.description: The lead's last message waits for a human reply, or an inline item is open.

openItems.description:
The inline items still open, oldest first, however far back: the chat may not have their page loaded. Absent
when none is (and from older hubs).

ProjectInspect.description: What a project's checkout or repository says: the default branch, CI and merge rules, and one line on what the lead will need.

leadNeeds.description: One line for a person, e.g. "no CI found: the merge train holds its PRs until the repo has CI".

notes.description: What could not be read, e.g. "branch rules need admin access on acme/storefront".

repo.description: Absent for a checkout without a GitHub remote.

oneOf.description: The machine's node is not connected.
No connected machine runs agents.
gh is missing or logged out where it ran.
gh is logged in but cannot see the repository (private, renamed, or a typo).
The path does not exist on the machine.
The path exists but is not a git checkout.
The clone destination exists. `CloneTarget.sameRemote` says whether it is already this repository.
git clone failed; the message is git's own last line.
The machine's node is older than this hub and cannot do this.

ProjectRef.description:
A project: a workspace with a lead and its own directory, on its home machine, where the lead runs. Its
`projectId` is the node's id for that directory, so the ref also addresses the files; the directory may be a git
repo or a plain folder. A project holds zero or more repos (`ProjectRepo`), each in a node directory of its
own or in the project's.

PromptScope.description: Which text is meant: the one shipped in the binary, the hub-wide override, or one project's override.

paused.description: true: dead agents there wait instead of resuming; false: they resume again.

taskIds.description: The agents whose deaths opened it, oldest first.

until.description: When it closes if nothing else dies there; an agent there completing closes it sooner.

RememberedItem.description: What a `remember` call wrote, as a line in the project's chat. Undone with `memory_undo`.

replaced.description: The whole entry it replaced, which Undo puts back.

RepoAdvancedData.description: `repo.advanced`: a node's fetch saw the remote's default branch move, so the hub reads the repo's merges now.

from.description: Absent on the first fetch the node saw.

by.description: Who answered it ("human:<device>"), once someone did.

workstreamId.description: The order it is about, when it is about one.

RequestKind.description:
What a lead needs a person for that chat can't carry safely: a secret value (entered in a masked field and sealed to
the sink's node, never in a transcript), or an approval of a risky command (a gated run, or a session's tool
prompt). The lead asks everything else in chat.

RequestState.description:
The state names of the chat items that show it (`SecretRequestState`, `CommandApprovalState`). secret: open →
stored | withdrawn. approval: open → approved → ran | failed, or open → denied; an approval the node could not run
goes back to open with the reason in `evidence`.

RunEnd.description: Why a run ended, so a node going away reads apart from a person stopping it. Set once the run is no longer active.

oneOf.description: The agent finished the turn.
Someone interrupted or stopped it: `RunInfo.endedBy` says who.
A steer cut it short at a tool boundary to take its own turn (`RunInfo.supersededBy`). Not a failure.
The node was stopping (SIGTERM) and cut it.
The node found it active on start: it died with the node process (crash, SIGKILL, power loss).
The machine slept and the agent's stream did not come back.
The agent's process exited or was killed with nobody asking; `failure` has the exit code or signal.
A usage, rate or pool limit; `failure.resetAt` says when to continue.
The conversation no longer fits in the model's context.
Any other failure; `failure.class` says which.
Set by the hub, never by a node: the watchdog saw no output for too long and ended the run.

SecretFingerprint.description: 8 lowercase hex characters: the sha256 prefix of the plaintext

SecretRequestItem.description:
The lead needs a secret. The app shows a masked field; the value never enters the transcript: it is sealed to the
sink's machine and answered with `secret_submit`, naming `requestId`. Only its fingerprint comes back.

by.description: The key name of the person who answered.

envName.description: An `env:` sink: the variable it writes, when not the one `name` gives (`secrets::secret_env_name`).

note.description: Why it is open again, or why it could not be stored.

text.description: One line: why the lead needs it.

SkillName.description: Lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, at most 64 characters

text.description: steer.queued: the first 120 characters, the mode and who sent it.

SteerMode.description: How a steer reaches a running agent.

oneOf.description:
Enter, "add to the lead's queue": taken in at the agent's next tool boundary, as its own turn. Never cuts a
running tool.
⌘Enter, "interrupt and redirect now": stops the current step and delivers at once.
The hub stored it, or put it in the offline queue.
claude's context took it in (`command_lifecycle started`).
The agent replied after taking it in, or a lead call named it (`--steer S12`).
Its run ended with no reply after it was delivered.
Dropped while still queued.
The machine stayed offline past the queue's TTL.

TableBlock.description: Rows of plain-text cells, one per column.

base.description: On `task.started` for a new worktree: where its branch started.

createdAt.description: When the task was spawned: a `task.started` for a task spawned before a turn is not that turn's start.

ThreadEventData.description: Fields `HubEvent.data` may carry on `thread.*` events, alongside whatever else the hub adds.

endCause.description:
Why the run ended: on `thread.completed`, `.failed`, `.interrupted` and `.usage_limited` from a node that
records it.

late.description: The run ended while the hub was down and this event was emitted on its return.

since.description: When the hub first saw it without an owner.

title.description: The session's title on its node.

ToolPermission.description:
An approval raised by a session's tool permission prompt instead of a gated command: answering it answers the prompt
on the project's node. Its machine is the request's project's.

summary.description: The command, the path, or the tool's own description.

TrainEventData.description:
The merge train's events: `change.queued`, `change.ready`, `change.needs_rebase`, `change.ci_failed`,
`change.refused`, `pr.merged`, `pr.merged_outside`. Which fields each carries is in
`HubEventType`'s docs.

authorKind.description: pr.merged_outside: who opened and who merged it, by the git host's account type.

base.description: pr.merged, pr.merged_outside: the branch it merged into.

batchPr.description: pr.merged: the train's batch PR it landed in.

ci.description: pr.merged on a repo with no CI: what fleetd checked instead.

head.description: pr.merged_outside: the PR's head branch and when it was opened.

mergedAt.description: pr.merged, pr.merged_outside: when it landed on the git host.

mergedBy.description: pr.merged_outside: the merger's login on the git host, so a merge by the person's own account is their touch.

taskId.description: pr.merged: the writer task whose PR it was, when a task wrote it.

UsageClass.description:
What stopped a turn. `usage_limit`: the plan's usage limit or a proxy's quota cooldown. `rate_limit`: a 429, or a
proxy resting its credentials after one.
`pool_exhausted`: the user's proxy has no account for the model; it waits for usage_resume.

UsageEventData.description: Fields `HubEvent.data` carries on usage.breaker and usage.resumed.

breakerCleared.description: usage.resumed: the breaker was open and is now closed.

by.description:
usage.resumed: "reset", "check" (fleetd tried one parked thread, or the one it tried completed a turn),
"unchecked" (nothing was left parked to try, so the pause lifted for the next turn to try the login), "turn" (a
turn on the login succeeded), or who ran usage_resume.

check.description:
usage.resumed: a check of an open breaker; the one thread listed is the one tried, and the breaker stays open
until its turn completes.

checkAt.description: usage.breaker: no reset named, so fleetd checks the login at this time.

proxy.description: usage.breaker: a proxy in front of the login decided the limit.

threads.description: usage.resumed: the threads sent "continue", in the order they were sent.

WebPreview.description:
How a project's web app is built and run for a preview, each command with `sh -c` in the preview's worktree and
the project's variables, as setup commands run (#501).

build.description: Builds the app; none for an app the start command builds itself.

inputs.description: Files whose contents decide what setup makes, such as lockfiles.

ready.description: Asked until it answers, for at most 2 minutes after the start.

setup.description:
Run first, in order: install dependencies, generate code. Skipped when `inputs` haven't changed since a
preview of this project last ran them on this machine.

start.description: Serves the app on `127.0.0.1:$PORT`; it runs until the preview ends.

WorkLandedData.description:
`HubEvent.data` on `work.landed`: a commit that reached a watched base, however it got there, and the fleetd work
it was.

changeId.description: The Change it is, or merged.

headBranch.description: The branch it came from, when the merge message or the host names one.

prNumber.description: The PR or merge request it came from, when the merge message or the host names one.

taskId.description: The write task whose work it is: its Change's, or the one whose branch it came from.

briefEdited.description: workstream.state: the brief was set or edited.

reason.description: workstream.state (stopped) and workstream.done: why, and who.

oneOf.description: A draft (no brief yet) or running: which one is the brief's to say. Older records read back as open.

WorktreeBase.description: Where a writer's worktree branch started: the remote's default branch, freshly fetched unless `error` says why not.

fetchedAt.description:
When `ref` was last fetched: by this start, else by the one whose copy it fell back to. Absent for a local
branch, or when git can't tell.

forkBehind.description:
A fork (an `upstream` remote beside it) only: the commits upstream's default branch has that `ref` lacks, as
last fetched.

ref.description: "origin/main"; a local branch when there is no remote, or no copy of the remote's.
